title: EPA/ARS/NAREL radiological data determinations, Hunters Point Naval Shipyard Superfund Site (Nov. 2024 and Mar. 2026) (Us Epa's Narel)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request concerns two laboratory incidents involving radiological samples collected from the Hunters Point Naval Shipyard Superfund site in San Francisco, California, and analyzed by the Navy contractor American Radiation Services (“ARS”), a subsidiary of The Heal Group. Both incidents involved EPA review of ARS sampling results, including determinations by NAREL.

First incident (November 2024): ARS reported a detection of plutonium-239 (Pu-239) in an air sample collected above Parcel C. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s National Air and Radiation Environmental Laboratory (“NAREL”) subsequently deemed that detection to be the result of contamination within the laboratory.

Second incident (March 2026): ARS reported detections of multiple radiological isotopes in air and soil samples collected at Parcels B and C. NAREL again deemed these detections invalid, attributing the rejection to an alleged “inappropriate quality control method.”

The basis for, and circumstances surrounding, each of these two determinations is the central subject of this request.

Records Requested
For each of the two incidents described above, the requester seeks all of the following records:

Case-initiation or referral documentation — records opening, assigning, or referring any review, inquiry, investigation, or re-analysis of either incident.
Investigative memoranda and analyses concerning either incident.
Status reports, updates, briefings, and tracking records concerning either incident.
Records documenting the basis for each determination — for the November 2024 finding that the Pu-239 detection resulted from laboratory contamination, and for the March 2026 finding that the detections were invalid due to an “inappropriate quality control method.” This includes the underlying sample and instrument data; the quality-assurance/quality-control standard operating procedures and data-validation acceptance criteria applied; any reanalysis, re-sampling, or confirmatory testing; and records identifying the personnel who made, reviewed, and approved each determination.
Laboratory audit and data-validation materials, including NAREL bench records, chain-of-custody documentation, instrument calibration and QC records, validation packages, and any audit or assessment of ARS’s analytical work.
Internal communications within and among EPA components (including Region 9, the Office of Radiation and Indoor Air, and NAREL) concerning either incident.
Communications with American Radiation Services and/or The Heal Group concerning either incident or the underlying samples.
EPA communications with the Department of the Navy (including NAVFAC and BRAC Program Management Office West) concerning either incident.
EPA communications with the California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), the San Francisco Department of Public Health (SFDPH), the Office of the San Francisco Board of Supervisors for District 10, and the Office of the Mayor of San Francisco concerning either incident.
Contractor-oversight assessments and related records concerning ARS’s performance in connection with either incident.
Records referencing data-integrity protocols, re-sampling protocols, or oversight measures at Hunters Point adopted or applied in light of prior contractor data-quality issues at the site, to the extent they relate to either incident.

Components and Custodians
Please search at least the following components, and any others reasonably likely to hold responsive records:
EPA Region 9 (San Francisco) — Superfund Division / Federal Facilities program staff responsible for Hunters Point.
Office of Radiation and Indoor Air (ORIA).
National Air and Radiation Environmental Laboratory (NAREL), Montgomery, Alabama — including the analysts, reviewers, and managers involved in the two determinations.

Time Period
This request covers records created or received from November 1, 2024 through the date the search for responsive records is conducted.

Definition of “Records”
“Records” is intended in its broadest sense and includes, without limitation: emails and their attachments; instant and text messages (including Microsoft Teams, Slack, and SMS); memoranda; reports; presentations; meeting notes and calendar entries; letters; data files and spreadsheets; laboratory bench records, chain-of-custody forms, quality-control and quality-assurance records; raw and processed instrument data; and any drafts of the foregoing.

Form and Format of Production
Please provide responsive records in native electronic format wherever practicable (for example, spreadsheets as .xlsx rather than PDF, and laboratory data in its native file format), together with associated metadata. Where native production is not feasible, searchable PDF is acceptable. Electronic delivery by email or secure file transfer is preferred.

Fee Category and Fee Waiver
The requester, Greg Schwartz, is an independent investigative journalist whose work is published by CounterPunch and other outlets. He therefore qualifies as a representative of the news media within the meaning of 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii). Fees should accordingly be limited to reasonable standard charges for document duplication, and no search or review fees should be assessed. The requester gathers these records to report on a matter of public concern and intends to distribute the resulting information to the public through his published reporting.
The requester additionally seeks a waiver of all fees pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii). Disclosure of these records is in the public interest because it will contribute significantly to public understanding of how EPA evaluated, validated, or invalidated radiological sampling results at a federal Superfund site adjacent to a densely populated community, and of the adequacy of contractor oversight at that site. The requester has no commercial interest in the records and will disseminate any information obtained to the public through his journalism.

Request for Expedited Processing
The requester asks that this request be granted expedited processing under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(E). There is a compelling need: the records concern potential radiological contamination at a site bordering residential neighborhoods, and there is an urgent need to inform the public about actual or alleged government activity affecting public health and safety. If expedited processing is denied, the requester asks for a written explanation and reserves the right to appeal that denial.

Segregability and Withholdings
Please release all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions of any responsive record. For any record or portion withheld, please identify the specific FOIA exemption claimed and provide an index or description sufficient to allow the requester to evaluate the basis for the withholding. The requester reserves the right to appeal any withholding, any adverse determination, and any inadequacy in the search.

Conclusion
If any part of this request is unclear, or if narrowing any category would assist in processing, please contact me before denying or substantially limiting the request so that we may discuss it. I look forward to your acknowledgment within the statutory time period.

Sincerely,
Greg Schwartz
Independent Investigative Journalist
17 Merrydale Road, APT 12, San Rafael, CA 94903
greg.m.schwartz@gmail.com  |  (216) 394-6572

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Greg Schwartz
